reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about reduction kinetics, nucleation, and phase formation, but no cited evidence is provided to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific synchronization of five noble metal precursors or the direct link between reduction timing and high-entropy alloy phase stability in nanoparticles.
premises: Simultaneous reduction of all metal precursors is achievable with a strong reducing agent and carefully chosen ligands at 80–120 °C
Synchronized reduction leads to homogeneous nucleation and congruent growth
Homogeneous nucleation locks all elements into a single solid-solution phase before phase separation can occur
Staggered reduction kinetics cause phase separation, compositional gradients, and defect-rich interfaces
The hypothesis applies specifically to noble metal systems (Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru, Ir) under moderate-temperature, ligand-controlled conditions
